Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From ec6ce7075ef879b91a8710829016005dc8170f17 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Peter Korsgaard <peter@korsgaard.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2024 12:06:35 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] usb: gadget: composite: fix OS descriptors w_value logic

The OS descriptors logic had the high/low byte of w_value inverted, causing
the extended properties to not be accessible for interface != 0.

>From the Microsoft documentation:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/usbcon/microsoft-os-1-0-descriptors-specification

OS_Desc_CompatID.doc (w_index = 0x4):

- wValue:

  High Byte = InterfaceNumber.  InterfaceNumber is set to the number of the
  interface or function that is associated with the descriptor, typically
  0x00.  Because a device can have only one extended compat ID descriptor,
  it should ignore InterfaceNumber, regardless of the value, and simply
  return the descriptor.

  Low Byte = 0.  PageNumber is used to retrieve descriptors that are larger
  than 64 KB.  The header section is 16 bytes, so PageNumber is set to 0 for
  this request.

We currently do not support >64KB compat ID descriptors, so verify that the
low byte is 0.

OS_Desc_Ext_Prop.doc (w_index = 0x5):

- wValue:

  High byte = InterfaceNumber.  The high byte of wValue is set to the number
  of the interface or function that is associated with the descriptor.

  Low byte = PageNumber.  The low byte of wValue is used to retrieve
  descriptors that are larger than 64 KB.  The header section is 10 bytes, so
  PageNumber is set to 0 for this request.

We also don't support >64KB extended properties, so verify that the low byte
is 0 and use the high byte for the interface number.

Fixes: 37a3a533429e ("usb: gadget: OS Feature Descriptors support")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Peter Korsgaard <peter@korsgaard.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240404100635.3215340-1-peter@korsgaard.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/gadget/composite.c b/drivers/usb/gadget/composite.c
index 0ace45b66a31..0e151b54aae8 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/gadget/composite.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/gadget/composite.c
@@ -2112,7 +2112,7 @@ composite_setup(struct usb_gadget *gadget, const struct usb_ctrlrequest *ctrl)
 			buf[5] = 0x01;
 			switch (ctrl->bRequestType & USB_RECIP_MASK) {
 			case USB_RECIP_DEVICE:
-				if (w_index != 0x4 || (w_value >> 8))
+				if (w_index != 0x4 || (w_value & 0xff))
 					break;
 				buf[6] = w_index;
 				/* Number of ext compat interfaces */
@@ -2128,9 +2128,9 @@ composite_setup(struct usb_gadget *gadget, const struct usb_ctrlrequest *ctrl)
 				}
 				break;
 			case USB_RECIP_INTERFACE:
-				if (w_index != 0x5 || (w_value >> 8))
+				if (w_index != 0x5 || (w_value & 0xff))
 					break;
-				interface = w_value & 0xFF;
+				interface = w_value >> 8;
 				if (interface >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES ||
 				    !os_desc_cfg->interface[interface])
 					break;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/usb/gadget/composite.c`**
1. **Line 2112**: The condition checking for `w_value` was modified from `(w_value >> 8)` to `(w_value & 0xff)` for the case when `w_index` is `0x4`. This change ensures that the low byte of `w_value` is checked instead of the high byte.
   
2. **Line 2128**: Similarly, the condition for `w_index` being `0x5` was changed from `(w_value >> 8)` to `(w_value & 0xff)`. This ensures that the low byte is checked for this case as well.

3. **Line 2129**: The assignment of `interface` was changed from `interface = w_value & 0xFF` to `interface = w_value >> 8`, which correctly assigns the high byte of `w_value` to the `interface` variable.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `composite.c` file are related to fixing the logic for handling OS descriptors in USB gadget functionality. The changes ensure that the correct bytes of `w_value` are used according to the specifications outlined in the Microsoft documentation. Specifically, the high byte of `w_value` is now correctly used to determine the interface number, while the low byte is verified to be zero, which aligns with the requirements for both the extended compatibility ID descriptor and the extended properties descriptor. This fix addresses the bug where extended properties were not accessible for interfaces other than zero, thereby improving the overall functionality of the USB gadget driver.


The bug occurs because the logic incorrectly checks the high byte of `w_value` instead of the low byte for the conditions related to the OS descriptors. This inversion leads to improper handling of the interface number, making extended properties inaccessible for interfaces other than zero.

```c
if (w_index != 0x4 || (w_value & 0xff))
```

```c

```
```c
interface = w_value >> 8;
```
Reason:
The fix corrects the checks to use the low byte of `w_value` for the conditions, ensuring that the interface number is properly handled. This aligns the implementation with the Microsoft specifications for USB OS descriptors, allowing access to extended properties for the correct interfaces.
